claim: The Notch signaling pathway uses families of ligands and receptors to transmit signals to nearby cells.
source: The Notch signaling pathway uses families of ligands and receptors to transmit signals to nearby cells.
evidence: This is a general statement about the Notch pathway that is supported by established scientific knowledge and is stated in the abstract.

claim: Notch pathway components are expressed in diverse combinations in different cell types.
source: These components are expressed in diverse combinations in different cell types, interact in a many-to-many fashion, both within the same cell (in cis) and between cells (in trans), and their interactions are modulated by Fringe glycosyltransferases.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge about Notch pathway expression patterns.

claim: Notch pathway components interact in a many-to-many fashion both within the same cell (in cis) and between cells (in trans).
source: These components are expressed in diverse combinations in different cell types, interact in a many-to-many fashion, both within the same cell (in cis) and between cells (in trans), and their interactions are modulated by Fringe glycosyltransferases.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge about Notch pathway interactions.

claim: Notch pathway interactions are modulated by Fringe glycosyltransferases.
source: These components are expressed in diverse combinations in different cell types, interact in a many-to-many fashion, both within the same cell (in cis) and between cells (in trans), and their interactions are modulated by Fringe glycosyltransferases.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge about Fringe modulation of Notch signaling.

claim: All four ligands (Dll1, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2) were able to bind receptors in cis and in trans.
source: All four ligands were able to bind receptors in cis and in trans, and all ligands trans-activated both receptors, although Jag1-Notch1 signaling was substantially weaker than other ligand-receptor combinations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the binding and signaling assays described in the manuscript.

claim: All ligands trans-activated both Notch1 and Notch2 receptors.
source: All four ligands were able to bind receptors in cis and in trans, and all ligands trans-activated both receptors, although Jag1-Notch1 signaling was substantially weaker than other ligand-receptor combinations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from trans-activation assays shown in Figure 2.

claim: Jag1-Notch1 signaling was substantially weaker than other ligand-receptor combinations.
source: All four ligands were able to bind receptors in cis and in trans, and all ligands trans-activated both receptors, although Jag1-Notch1 signaling was substantially weaker than other ligand-receptor combinations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from trans-activation assays shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cis-interactions were predominantly inhibitory, with the exception of the Dll1- and Dll4-Notch2 pairs.
source: Cis-interactions were predominantly inhibitory, with the exception of the Dll1- and Dll4-Notch2 pairs, which exhibited cis-activation stronger than trans-activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cis-activation and cis-modulation assays shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Dll1-Notch2 and Dll4-Notch2 pairs exhibited cis-activation stronger than trans-activation.
source: Cis-interactions were predominantly inhibitory, with the exception of the Dll1- and Dll4-Notch2 pairs, which exhibited cis-activation stronger than trans-activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing cis-activation and trans-activation shown in Figures 4B and 5A.

claim: Lfng strengthened Delta-mediated trans-activation for both Notch1 and Notch2 receptors.
source: Lfng strengthened Delta-mediated trans-activation and weakened Jagged-mediated trans-activation for both receptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from trans-activation assays with Lfng shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Lfng weakened Jagged-mediated trans-activation for both Notch1 and Notch2 receptors.
source: Lfng strengthened Delta-mediated trans-activation and weakened Jagged-mediated trans-activation for both receptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from trans-activation assays with Lfng shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cis-ligands showed diverse cis-inhibition strengths, which depended on the identity of the trans-ligand as well as the receptor.
source: Finally, cis-ligands showed diverse cis-inhibition strengths, which depended on the identity of the trans-ligand as well as the receptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cis-modulation assays shown in Figure 6.

claim: The Notch pathway consists of four receptors (Notch1–4) in mammals.
source: In mammals, the Notch pathway consists of four receptors (Notch1–4), four canonical activating ligands (Dll1, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2), at least one predominantly inhibitory ligand (Dll3), and non-canonical ligands (D'Souza et al., 2008; Falix et al., 2012; Fiddes et al., 2018; Gera and Dighe, 2018; Ladi et al., 2005; Serth et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Notch pathway consists of four canonical activating ligands (Dll1, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2) in mammals.
source: In mammals, the Notch pathway consists of four receptors (Notch1–4), four canonical activating ligands (Dll1, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2), at least one predominantly inhibitory ligand (Dll3), and non-canonical ligands (D'Souza et al., 2008; Falix et al., 2012; Fiddes et al., 2018; Gera and Dighe, 2018; Ladi et al., 2005; Serth et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Dll3 is at least one predominantly inhibitory ligand in the Notch pathway.
source: In mammals, the Notch pathway consists of four receptors (Notch1–4), four canonical activating ligands (Dll1, Dll4, Jag1, and Jag2), at least one predominantly inhibitory ligand (Dll3), and non-canonical ligands (D'Souza et al., 2008; Falix et al., 2012; Fiddes et al., 2018; Gera and Dighe, 2018; Ladi et al., 2005; Serth et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ligands and receptors interact both within the same cell (in cis) and between adjacent cells (in trans).
source: Ligands and receptors interact both within the same cell (in cis) and between adjacent cells (in trans).
evidence: This is a general statement about Notch pathway interactions supported by established knowledge.

claim: Either cis or trans configuration has the potential to activate or inhibit signaling.
source: Either configuration has the potential to activate or inhibit signaling (del Álamo et al., 2011; Nandagopal et al., 2019; Sprinzak et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The level of signaling in a Notch-expressing cell generally depends on which ligand, receptor, and Fringe variants are expressed in the cell and its neighbors.
source: The level of signaling in a Notch-expressing cell generally depends on which ligand, receptor, and Fringe variants are expressed in the cell and its neighbors.
evidence: This is a general statement about Notch signaling that is supported by established knowledge and the experimental results in this manuscript.

claim: Notch pathway components are expressed in various combinations in different cell types, often including coexpression of ligands, receptors, and at least one Fringe enzyme.
source: These components are expressed in various combinations in different cell types, often including coexpression of ligands, receptors, and at least one Fringe enzyme (Granados et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Transcriptional responses are sensitive to the amplitude and duration of Notch signaling.
source: Transcriptional responses are sensitive to the amplitude and duration of Notch signaling (Falo-Sanjuan et al., 2019; Kuang et al., 2020; Nandagopal et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In the canonical trans-activation mechanism, binding of ligands on one cell to receptors on an adjacent cell triggers ligand endocytosis.
source: In the canonical trans-activation mechanism, binding of ligands on one cell to receptors on an adjacent cell triggers ligand endocytosis, which generates mechanical strain on the receptor, exposing a metalloproteinase recognition site (Langridge and Struhl, 2017; Lovendahl et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature describing the canonical Notch activation mechanism.

claim: Ligand endocytosis generates mechanical strain on the receptor, exposing a metalloproteinase recognition site.
source: In the canonical trans-activation mechanism, binding of ligands on one cell to receptors on an adjacent cell triggers ligand endocytosis, which generates mechanical strain on the receptor, exposing a metalloproteinase recognition site (Langridge and Struhl, 2017; Lovendahl et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature describing the canonical Notch activation mechanism.

claim: S2 cleavage by ADAM10 results in shedding of the receptor extracellular domain (NECD).
source: S2 cleavage by ADAM10 results in shedding of the receptor extracellular domain (NECD) and permits a subsequent S3 cleavage by γ-secretase to release the Notch intracellular domain (NICD).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about Notch signaling mechanism supported by general knowledge.

claim: S3 cleavage by γ-secretase releases the Notch intracellular domain (NICD).
source: S2 cleavage by ADAM10 results in shedding of the receptor extracellular domain (NECD) and permits a subsequent S3 cleavage by γ-secretase to release the Notch intracellular domain (NICD).
evidence: This is a well-established fact about Notch signaling mechanism supported by general knowledge.

claim: The free NICD directly translocates into the nucleus and binds cofactors MAML and RBPjκ to activate target genes.
source: The free NICD directly translocates into the nucleus and binds cofactors MAML and RBPjκ to activate target genes.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about Notch signaling mechanism supported by general knowledge.

claim: Downstream target genes respond similarly to NICD originating from the Notch1 or Notch2 receptors.
source: Downstream target genes respond similarly to NICD originating from the Notch1 or Notch2 receptors (Kraman and McCright, 2005; Liu et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Downstream target genes respond differently to distinct concentrations of NICD.
source: However, they respond differently to distinct concentrations of NICD.
evidence: This claim is supported by the context and citations in the surrounding text.

claim: In pancreatic progenitors, complete Notch inhibition permitted differentiation, low levels of NICD promoted proliferation, and higher levels induced quiescence.
source: In pancreatic progenitors (Ninov et al., 2012) and central nervous system stem cells (Guentchev and McKay, 2006), complete Notch inhibition permitted differentiation, low levels of NICD promoted proliferation, and higher levels induced quiescence.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In central nervous system stem cells, complete Notch inhibition permitted differentiation, low levels of NICD promoted proliferation, and higher levels induced quiescence.
source: In pancreatic progenitors (Ninov et al., 2012) and central nervous system stem cells (Guentchev and McKay, 2006), complete Notch inhibition permitted differentiation, low levels of NICD promoted proliferation, and higher levels induced quiescence.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Notch signaling amplitude can influence the timing of developmental transitions, with higher NICD concentrations activating master transcription factors earlier than lower concentrations.
source: Notch signaling amplitude can also influence the timing of developmental transitions, with higher NICD concentrations activating master transcription factors earlier than lower concentrations, depending on the target's enhancer architecture (Falo-Sanjuan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Fringe enzymes can alter receptor-ligand binding and activation strengths, sometimes in opposite directions.
source: Fringe enzymes can alter receptor-ligand binding and activation strengths, sometimes in opposite directions (Hicks et al., 2000; Kakuda et al., 2020; Kakuda and Haltiwanger, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Upregulating expression of a ligand can suppress Notch signaling cell-autonomously through a process termed cis-inhibition.
source: Upregulating expression of a ligand can suppress Notch signaling cell-autonomously, through a process termed cis-inhibition (Becam et al., 2010; Fiuza et al., 2010; Sprinzak et al., 2010; Thambyrajah et al., 2024), or trans-activate receptors on neighboring cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In some cases, ligands can also activate signaling by receptors in the same cell.
source: In some cases, ligands can also activate signaling by receptors in the same cell (Nandagopal et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Some ligands can inhibit signaling intercellularly ('trans-inhibition') by binding receptors strongly without activating them.
source: Finally, growing evidence suggests that some ligands can inhibit signaling intercellularly ('trans-inhibition') by binding receptors strongly without activating them (Benedito et al., 2009; Golson et al., 2009; Luna-Escalante et al., 2018), as may be the case for Jag1 and Lunatic Fringe (Lfng)-modified Notch1 (Hicks et al., 2000; Kakuda and Haltiwanger, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Jag1 and Lunatic Fringe (Lfng)-modified Notch1 may exhibit trans-inhibition.
source: Finally, growing evidence suggests that some ligands can inhibit signaling intercellularly ('trans-inhibition') by binding receptors strongly without activating them (Benedito et al., 2009; Golson et al., 2009; Luna-Escalante et al., 2018), as may be the case for Jag1 and Lunatic Fringe (Lfng)-modified Notch1 (Hicks et al., 2000; Kakuda and Haltiwanger, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and is presented as a possibility.

claim: CHO-K1 cells exhibit negligible endogenous expression levels of Notch receptors and ligands, and no endogenous Notch signaling activity.
source: As a base cell line, we used CHO-K1 cells, which exhibit negligible endogenous expression levels of Notch receptors and ligands, and no endogenous Notch signaling activity (Supplementary file 1; Singh et al., 2018; Sprinzak et al., 2010).

claim: Receiver cells expressed a chimeric human Notch receptor, whose intracellular domain was replaced with a minimal Gal4 transcription factor.
source: These cells expressed a chimeric human Notch receptor, whose intracellular domain was replaced with a minimal Gal4 transcription factor ('Gal4esn', henceforth denoted Gal4).

claim: Cotranslational mTurq2 reporter expression correlated with surface receptor expression.
source: Expression of the cotranslational mTurq2 reporter was broadly comparable between different receiver clones (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), and correlated with surface receptor expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).

claim: Almost all ligands signaled more strongly to Notch2 than to Notch1, regardless of Fringe expression.

source: The exception was Dll4, which signaled more strongly to Notch1 than Notch2 in the dLfng condition, but activated Notch1 and Notch2 to similar levels with Lfng.

claim: Dll4 activated Notch1 and Notch2 to similar levels with Lfng.
source: The exception was Dll4, which signaled more strongly to Notch1 than Notch2 in the dLfng condition, but activated Notch1 and Notch2 to similar levels with Lfng.

source: Second, Notch1 and Notch2 responded in a qualitatively similar way to Lfng, as can be seen by plotting signaling strengths for the Lfng condition vs. those for dLfng (Figure 2B and C).

claim: Lfng significantly enhanced Notch1 and Notch2 trans-activation by both Dll1 and Dll4.
source: Lfng significantly enhanced Notch1 and Notch2 trans-activation by both Dll1 and Dll4.

claim: Lfng significantly decreased trans-activation of both receptors by Jag2 (~1.4-fold).
source: Lfng significantly decreased trans-activation of both receptors by Jag1 (>2.5-fold) and, to a lesser extent, Jag2 (~1.4-fold).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In the absence of Fringe expression (i.e. with dLfng), Dll1-Notch1 signaling strength was only slightly above background.
source: In the absence of Fringe expression (i.e. with dLfng), Dll1-Notch1 signaling strength was only slightly above background (Figure 2A).

source: By contrast, Dll4 activated Notch1 9-fold more strongly than Dll1 in the dLfng condition, consistent with previous results from E14TG2a mouse embryonic stem cells (Tveriakhina et al., 2018), possibly reflecting the ~10-fold greater binding affinity of Notch1 to the Dll4 extracellular domain (ECD), compared to the Dll1 ECD (Andrawes et al., 2013).

claim: Notch1 has ~10-fold greater binding affinity to the Dll4 extracellular domain (ECD), compared to the Dll1 ECD.
source: By contrast, Dll4 activated Notch1 9-fold more strongly than Dll1 in the dLfng condition, consistent with previous results from E14TG2a mouse embryonic stem cells (Tveriakhina et al., 2018), possibly reflecting the ~10-fold greater binding affinity of Notch1 to the Dll4 extracellular domain (ECD), compared to the Dll1 ECD (Andrawes et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Lfng expression increased Dll1 signaling more than Dll4, reducing the difference in signaling strengths between the ligands to 2.7-fold.
source: Lfng expression increased Dll1 signaling more than Dll4, reducing the difference in signaling strengths between the ligands to 2.7-fold (Figure 2A).

claim: Jag1 signaled to Notch2 at levels comparable to those of Dll1 in the dLfng condition.

claim: Endogenous Fringes showed overall weaker effects on signaling activity than transfected Lfng did.

claim: Endogenous Lfng modestly weakens Jagged signaling and strengthens Dll1-Notch1 signaling.

claim: Jag1 senders activated Notch1 receivers poorly, despite activating Notch2 receivers well.

claim: Notch2 receivers were activated to a similar extent by Jag1 and Dll1 senders (<1.5-fold difference).

claim: Cis-inhibition by Jag2 was observed with Notch2.

claim: Dll4 and Jag2 cis-inhibited Notch1 reporter activity in C2C12-Nkd cells relative to the NGFR cis-ligand negative control.

claim: No cis-activation by Dll4 was observed in C2C12-Nkd.

claim: Weak trans-activation of Notch1 by Jag1 is likely to be an intrinsic property of these ligands and receptors.

claim: Strong cis-activation of Notch2 by Dll1 and Dll4 is likely to be an intrinsic property of these ligands and receptors.

evidence: This claim is inferred from the consistency of results across CHO-K1 and C2C12 cell lines.

claim: Ligand class (Delta vs. Jagged) did not predict the signaling level with either receptor.
source: Ligand class (Delta vs. Jagged) did not predict the signaling level with either receptor.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing diverse signaling strengths across ligand-receptor combinations.

claim: Ligand class correlated strongly with the sign of response to Lfng, which respectively increased or decreased signaling by Delta or Jagged ligands to both receptors.
source: However, it did correlate strongly with the sign of response to Lfng, which respectively increased or decreased signaling by Delta or Jagged ligands to both receptors (Figure 2C).

claim: There was striking uniformity in the ultrasensitivity of Notch responses, which was roughly constant across ligand-receptor-Fringe combinations.

claim: Delta ligands cis-inhibited only Notch1, and cis-activated Notch2 at levels exceeding the maximal Notch2 trans-signaling observed here.

claim: Jagged ligands cis-inhibited both Notch1 and Notch2 receptors.

claim: Cis- and trans-activation may involve different molecular mechanisms.
source: Notably, Lfng had different impacts on cis- and trans-interactions for some ligand-receptor combinations such as Jag1-Notch2 and Jag2-Notch2 (Figure 5D), suggesting the possibility that cis- and trans-activation may involve different molecular mechanisms.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the observation of different Lfng effects on cis- and trans-interactions.

claim: Lfng-dependent trans-inhibition of Notch1 by Jag1 has been shown to play a key role in angiogenesis, where it inhibits Dll4-Notch1 signaling.
source: Lfng-dependent trans-inhibition of Notch1 by Jag1 has been shown to play a key role in some contexts such as angiogenesis, where it inhibits Dll4-Notch1 signaling (Benedito et al., 2009; Pedrosa et al., 2015) and the embryonic pancreas, where it inhibits Dll1-Notch1 signaling (Golson et al., 2009).

claim: Lfng-dependent trans-inhibition of Notch1 by Jag1 has been shown to play a key role in the embryonic pancreas, where it inhibits Dll1-Notch1 signaling.
source: Lfng-dependent trans-inhibition of Notch1 by Jag1 has been shown to play a key role in some contexts such as angiogenesis, where it inhibits Dll4-Notch1 signaling (Benedito et al., 2009; Pedrosa et al., 2015) and the embryonic pancreas, where it inhibits Dll1-Notch1 signaling (Golson et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Trans-inhibition could result from the combination of strong binding with weak activation, which was most pronounced for Jag1-Notch1.
source: Our results explain how trans-inhibition could result from the combination of strong binding with weak activation, which was most pronounced for Jag1-Notch1 (Figure 2A, Figure 3B, and Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2A, 3B, and 6C.

claim: Lfng increased Jag1 binding to Notch1.
source: Further, this effect was enhanced by Lfng, which increased binding strength in the ligand binding assay (Figure 3H), while decreasing signaling in both the coculture and plated ligand assays (Figures 2C and 3I), consistent with previous observations (Hicks et al., 2000; Kakuda and Haltiwanger, 2017; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Lfng decreased Jag1-Notch1 signaling in both the coculture and plated ligand assays.
source: Further, this effect was enhanced by Lfng, which increased binding strength in the ligand binding assay (Figure 3H), while decreasing signaling in both the coculture and plated ligand assays (Figures 2C and 3I), consistent with previous observations (Hicks et al., 2000; Kakuda and Haltiwanger, 2017; Taylor et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2C and 3I.

claim: Trans-inhibition may be a core function of Jag1.
source: These results suggest that Notch1 trans-inhibition may be a core function of Jag1, and could help explain the sometimes divergent behavior of Jag1 mutants compared with other ligands (Benedito et al., 2009; Chrysostomou et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results and citations to previous literature.

claim: Positive Jag1-Notch1 signaling is functionally important in some contexts, since weak signaling from Jag1-expressing OP9 cells prevents T-cell progenitors from differentiating into the B-cell lineage.
source: However, it is possible that positive Jag1-Notch1 signaling is also functionally important in some contexts, since weak signaling from Jag1-expressing OP9 cells prevents T-cell progenitors from differentiating into the B-cell lineage, in contrast with no-ligand controls (Lehar et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous literature and involves speculation about functional importance.

claim: When strongly cis-activating ligands compete with strongly trans-activating ligands, they cause no net decrease in signaling, as observed when cis-Delta ligands interact with Notch2.
source: For example, when strongly cis-activating ligands compete with strongly trans-activating ligands, they cause no net decrease in signaling, as observed when cis-Delta ligands interact with Notch2 (Figure 4B, Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4B and 6A and is consistent with the competitive binding model.

claim: When a strongly binding cis-ligand produces a weak or inactive complex, it can cis-inhibit.
source: By contrast, when a strongly binding cis-ligand produces a weak or inactive complex, it can cis-inhibit.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results and is consistent with the competitive binding model.

claim: Combinations that did not cis-activate (Jagged-Notch1) showed relatively stronger cis-inhibition than combinations that cis-activated weakly (Delta-Notch1, Jag1-Notch2).
source: In general, combinations that did not cis-activate (Jagged-Notch1) showed relatively stronger cis-inhibition than combinations that cis-activated weakly (Delta-Notch1, Jag1-Notch2) (Figure 6C, Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6C and 5A.

claim: Cis-Jag2-Notch1 was the strongest cis-inhibiting combination overall.
source: Cis-Jag2-Notch1 was the strongest cis-inhibiting combination overall.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Cis-Jag2-Notch1 could operate in a 'mutual inactivation' regime in which a cis-ligand titrates the receptor levels available to potential trans-activating ligands.
source: Because of its unique attributes of strong binding and weak cis-activation, cis-Jag2-Notch1 could operate in a 'mutual inactivation' regime in which a cis-ligand titrates the receptor levels available to potential trans-activating ligands (LeBon et al., 2014; Sprinzak et al., 2010; Xu et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results and citations to previous literature.

claim: For Notch1, each type of ligand had a comparative advantage in its ability to cis-inhibit trans-activation by itself compared to other ligands.
source: Strikingly, for Notch1, each type of ligand had a comparative advantage in its ability to cis-inhibit trans-activation by itself compared to other ligands (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Dll1 cis-inhibited trans-Dll1 signaling more efficiently than trans-Jag2.
source: For example, Dll1 cis-inhibited trans-Dll1 signaling more efficiently than trans-Jag2, while Jag2 cis-inhibited trans-Jag2 signaling more efficiently than trans-Dll1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Jag2 cis-inhibited trans-Jag2 signaling more efficiently than trans-Dll1.
source: For example, Dll1 cis-inhibited trans-Dll1 signaling more efficiently than trans-Jag2, while Jag2 cis-inhibited trans-Jag2 signaling more efficiently than trans-Dll1.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Lfng increased Dll1-Notch1 and Dll4-Notch1 signaling by 3.3-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, in both cis-activation and trans-activation assays.
source: Lfng significantly increased Dll1-Notch1 and Dll4-Notch1 signaling by 3.3-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, in both assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Lfng had no effect on cis-activation of Notch1 by Jag1 and Jag2, which remained negligible with or without Lfng.
source: By contrast, Lfng had no effect on cis-activation of Notch1 by Jag1 and Jag2, which remained negligible with or without Lfng.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Despite its ability to increase Dll1 and Dll4 trans-activation of Notch2, Lfng did not strongly affect cis-activation.
source: Despite its ability to increase Dll1 and Dll4 trans-activation of Notch2, Lfng did not strongly affect cis-activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Lfng sharply reduced Jag1-Notch2 trans-activation.
source: While Lfng sharply reduced Jag1-Notch2 trans-activation (Figure 2C), it had negligible effects on cis-activation by the same components (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Lfng had negligible effects on Jag1-Notch2 cis-activation.
source: While Lfng sharply reduced Jag1-Notch2 trans-activation (Figure 2C), it had negligible effects on cis-activation by the same components (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: For Jag2-Notch2, Lfng had weak effects on trans-activation, but reduced cis-activation by more than 2-fold.
source: Conversely, for Jag2-Notch2, Lfng had weak effects on trans-activation, but reduced cis-activation by more than 2-fold (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cis- and trans-activation mechanisms respond to Lfng similarly for Notch1, but differently for Notch2.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that cis- and trans-activation mechanisms respond to Lfng similarly for Notch1, but differently for Notch2.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Lfng strengthened Notch1 binding to Dll1 by 6.4-fold on average.
source: In agreement with the previous work, Lfng strengthened Notch1 binding to Dll1 and Jag1 by 6.4-fold and 2.8-fold on average, respectively (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Lfng strengthened Notch1 binding to Jag1 by 2.8-fold on average.
source: In agreement with the previous work, Lfng strengthened Notch1 binding to Dll1 and Jag1 by 6.4-fold and 2.8-fold on average, respectively (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Lfng modestly strengthened Notch1 binding to Jag2.
source: Lfng also modestly strengthened Notch1 binding to Jag2.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Lfng had relatively little effect on Dll4-Notch1 binding.
source: However, Lfng had relatively little effect on Dll4-Notch1 binding.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and H.

claim: Lfng strongly increased Dll1-Notch1 signaling in the plated ligand assay.
source: Lfng strongly increased Dll1-Notch1 signaling and weakened Jag1-Notch1 signaling in the plated ligand assay (Figure 3I), similar to results with expressed ligands (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Lfng weakened Jag1-Notch1 signaling in the plated ligand assay.
source: Lfng strongly increased Dll1-Notch1 signaling and weakened Jag1-Notch1 signaling in the plated ligand assay (Figure 3I), similar to results with expressed ligands (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Lfng had opposite effects on binding and activation of Notch1 by the same Jag1-ext-Fc fragment.
source: Thus, Lfng had opposite effects on binding and activation of Notch1 by the same Jag1-ext-Fc fragment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3H and 3I.

claim: By strengthening Jag1-Notch1 binding while decreasing activation, Lfng may allow Jag1 to competitively trans-inhibit Notch1 activation by other ligands.
source: By strengthening Jag1-Notch1 binding while decreasing activation, Lfng may allow Jag1 to competitively trans-inhibit Notch1 activation by other ligands (Figure 3J; Benedito et al., 2009; Golson et al., 2009; Pedrosa et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental results and citations to previous literature.

claim: With Dll1, Lfng strengthens both binding and activation of Notch1.
source: While they do not rule out additional effects of Lfng on binding affinity for Dll4-Notch1, these results together suggest that with Dll1, Lfng strengthens both binding and activation of Notch1, while with Jagged ligands it strengthens binding but instead weakens activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results shown in Figures 3G, 3H, and 3I.

claim: With Jagged ligands, Lfng strengthens binding but weakens activation of Notch1.
source: While they do not rule out additional effects of Lfng on binding affinity for Dll4-Notch1, these results together suggest that with Dll1, Lfng strengthens both binding and activation of Notch1, while with Jagged ligands it strengthens binding but instead weakens activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results shown in Figures 3G, 3H, and 3I.

claim: Notch1 exhibited no cis-activation for any of the ligands, except for a modest response to Dll4, of no more than 20% of maximal trans-activation.
source: Notch1 exhibited no cis-activation for any of the ligands, except for a modest response to Dll4, of no more than 20% of maximal trans-activation (Figure 4B, upper left), consistent with previous observations in wt CHO-K1 cells (Nandagopal et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Notch2 was cis-activated by both Dll1 and Dll4, to levels exceeding those produced by trans-activation by high-Dll1 senders.
source: By contrast, Notch2 was cis-activated by both Dll1 and Dll4, to levels exceeding those produced by trans-activation by high-Dll1 senders (Figure 4B, lower left, compare with trans-activation in Figure 4B, lower right).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Jagged ligands did not cis-activate Notch2 in the cis-activation assay.
source: Jagged ligands, on the other hand, did not cis-activate Notch2 in this assay (Figure 4B, lower left).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: All ligands cis-inhibited intercellular Dll1-Notch1 signaling, achieving 75–100% inhibition in the highest cis-ligand expression bin.
source: All ligands cis-inhibited intercellular Dll1-Notch1 signaling, achieving 75–100% inhibition in the highest cis-ligand expression bin (Figure 4B, upper right).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Intercellular Dll1-Notch2 signaling was cis-inhibited by Jag1 and Jag2, but not by Dll1 or Dll4.
source: By contrast, intercellular Dll1-Notch2 signaling was cis-inhibited by Jag1 and Jag2, but not by Dll1 or Dll4, whose cis-activation further increased Notch2 signaling (Figure 4B, lower right).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Dll1 and Dll4 cis-activation further increased Notch2 signaling.
source: By contrast, intercellular Dll1-Notch2 signaling was cis-inhibited by Jag1 and Jag2, but not by Dll1 or Dll4, whose cis-activation further increased Notch2 signaling (Figure 4B, lower right).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Notch1 and Notch2 reporter activities showed no dependence on expression of negative control proteins H2B-mCherry or NGFR-T2A-H2B-mCherry, in either the cis-activation or cis-modulation assay.
source: These results were not due to non-specific effects of ectopic cis protein expression, as Notch1 and Notch2 reporter activities showed no dependence on expression of negative control proteins H2B-mCherry or NGFR-T2A-H2B-mCherry, in either the cis-activation or cis-modulation assay (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: For Notch2-Dll1 and Notch2-Dll4, single-cell reporter activities correlated with cis-ligand expression, regardless of whether cells were preinduced at a high or low culture density.
source: For Notch2-Dll1 and Notch2-Dll4, single-cell reporter activities correlated with cis-ligand expression, regardless of whether cells were preinduced at a high or low culture density (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The correlation between cis-ligand expression and reporter activity rules out the possibility that Delta-Notch2 cis-activation signal arises from S3-cleavage of NEXT generated by intercellular signaling during the ligand preinduction phase.
source: Together, this analysis rules out the possibility that Delta-Notch2 cis-activation signal arises from S3-cleavage of NEXT generated by intercellular signaling during the ligand preinduction phase.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: For ligand-Notch1 interactions (cis+trans), trans-activation significantly contributed to the overall signaling strength observed in the experiments.
source: For ligand-Notch1 interactions (cis+trans), trans-activation significantly contributed to the overall signaling strength observed in our experiments (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: With Lfng, the combination of cis- and trans-interactions produced over twice the signaling activity from Dll1 or Dll4 compared to cis-interactions alone in the increasing phase of the dose-response curves.
source: With Lfng, the combination of cis- and trans-interactions produced over twice the signaling activity from Dll1 or Dll4 compared to cis-interactions alone in the increasing phase of the dose-response curves (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Trans-activation can increase Notch1 activity beyond the level produced by cis-activation alone.
source: This result indicates that trans-activation can increase Notch1 activity beyond the level produced by cis-activation alone.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: For Jag2-Notch1, in either dLfng or Lfng conditions, signaling was only observed with trans-interactions.
source: For Jag2-Notch1, in either dLfng or Lfng conditions, signaling was only observed with trans-interactions (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: For Jag1-Notch1, no activation was seen in the cis-activation or the cis-+trans-activation modes.
source: For Jag1-Notch1, no activation was seen in the cis-activation or the cis-+trans-activation modes, consistent with earlier results (Figure 2A, Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and earlier results.

claim: Of the four ligands, trans Jag2 modestly increased Notch2 signaling beyond the level achieved by cis-activation alone, by about 1.5-fold.
source: Of the four ligands, trans Jag2 modestly increased Notch2 signaling beyond the level achieved by cis-activation alone, by about 1.5-fold (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In all other ligand-Notch2 conditions, trans-ligands failed to increase signaling, suggesting that cis-activation alone is sufficient to explain the observed level of signaling in these cis+trans conditions.
source: In all other ligand-Notch2 conditions, trans-ligands failed to increase signaling, suggesting that cis-activation alone is sufficient to explain the observed level of signaling in these cis+trans conditions.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: With Jag1-Notch2, combined cis- and trans-signaling was slightly lower than cis-only signaling with Lfng, suggesting that trans-interactions may limit signaling from cis-activation in this case.
source: With Jag1-Notch2, combined cis- and trans-signaling was slightly lower than cis-only signaling with Lfng (Figure 5B), suggesting that trans-interactions may limit signaling from cis-activation in this case.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 5B and involves speculation.

claim: Cis- and trans-signaling combine differently across the ligand-receptor combinations.
source: Together, these results indicate that cis- and trans-signaling combine differently across the ligand-receptor combinations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Lfng's effects on Notch1 cis-activation quantitatively resembled those on trans-activation.
source: Effects of Lfng on Notch1 cis-activation (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 5) quantitatively resembled those on trans-activation (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 5, and Figure 5D.

claim: Lfng significantly increased Dll1-Notch1 and Dll4-Notch1 signaling by 3.3-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, in both cis-activation and trans-activation assays.
source: Lfng significantly increased Dll1-Notch1 and Dll4-Notch1 signaling by 3.3-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively, in both assays.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5D.

claim: With Notch2, Lfng's effects on cis- and trans-interactions diverged.
source: With Notch2, Lfng's effects on cis- and trans-interactions diverged (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Despite its ability to increase Dll1 and Dll4 trans-activation of Notch2, Lfng did not strongly affect cis-activation.
source: Despite its ability to increase Dll1 and Dll4 trans-activation of Notch2, Lfng did not strongly affect cis-activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: For Jag2-Notch2, Lfng had weak effects on trans-activation, but reduced cis-activation by more than 2-fold.
source: Conversely, for Jag2-Notch2, Lfng had weak effects on trans-activation, but reduced cis-activation by more than 2-fold (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The effects of cis-interactions were qualitatively similar across different trans-activating ligands.
source: The effects of cis-interactions were qualitatively similar across different trans-activating ligands (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In all cases, cis-Jagged ligands inhibited Notch1 and Notch2, while cis-Delta ligands inhibited Notch1 and activated Notch2.
source: In all cases, cis-Jagged ligands inhibited Notch1 and Notch2, while cis-Delta ligands inhibited Notch1 and activated Notch2 (Figures 6A and 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6A and 4B.

claim: Cis-inhibition strength depended on both cis-ligand and trans-ligand identity.
source: Quantitatively, cis-inhibition strength depended on both cis-ligand and trans-ligand identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Jag2 was the most effective Notch1 cis-inhibitor across all trans-ligands.
source: For example, Jag2 was the most effective Notch1 cis-inhibitor across all trans-ligands (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ligands' relative cis-inhibition strengths did not correlate well with trans-activation strengths.
source: Ligands' relative cis-inhibition strengths did not correlate well with trans-activation strengths (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Combinations with modest or strong cis-activating potentials, such as Dll4-Notch1, Dll1-Notch2, and Dll4-Notch2, showed relatively poor cis-inhibition efficiencies relative to trans-activation.
source: In general, combinations with modest or strong cis-activating potentials, such as Dll4-Notch1, Dll1-Notch2, and Dll4-Notch2 (Figure 5A), showed relatively poor cis-inhibition efficiencies relative to trans-activation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A and 6C.

claim: The non-cis-activating ligands, Jag1 and Jag2, showed strong cis-inhibition efficiencies relative to trans-activation for Notch1.
source: The converse was also true for Notch1: the non-cis-activating ligands, Jag1 and Jag2 (Figure 5A), showed strong cis-inhibition efficiencies relative to trans-activation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 5A and 6C.

claim: For Notch2, no ligands favored cis-inhibition over trans-activation.
source: For Notch2, no ligands favored cis-inhibition over trans-activation, consistent with the observation that all ligands can cis-activate Notch2 to some extent (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 6C and 5A.

claim: For Notch1, ligands' trans-adjusted cis-inhibition efficiencies showed diverse dependencies on the identity of the trans-ligand.
source: For Notch1, ligands' trans-adjusted cis-inhibition efficiencies showed diverse dependencies on the identity of the trans-ligand (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Each cis-ligand inhibited signaling from the trans-ligand of the same identity with an equal or greater efficiency than it inhibited other trans-ligands.
source: Notably, each cis-ligand inhibited signaling from the trans-ligand of the same identity with an equal or greater efficiency than it inhibited other trans-ligands.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Jag-Notch2 cis-inhibition was relatively uniform across different cis- and trans-ligand combinations, varying by no more than 2-fold between the strongest and weakest cis-inhibiting combinations.
source: In contrast to the variability of Notch1 cis-inhibition, Jag-Notch2 cis-inhibition was relatively uniform across different cis- and trans-ligand combinations, varying by no more than 2-fold between the strongest and weakest cis-inhibiting combinations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Cis-inhibition strengths for Notch1, and to a lesser extent, Notch2, depend on the interplay of trans-ligand, cis-ligand, and receptor.
source: Together, these results suggest that cis-inhibition strengths for Notch1, and to a lesser extent, Notch2, depend on the interplay of trans-ligand, cis-ligand, and receptor.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Hill coefficients for cis-inhibition ranged from ~0.75 to 1.5.
source: Hill coefficients ranged from ~0.75 to 1.5 (Figure 6E), below the values obtained for trans-activation by the same components (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Cis-inhibition is a less ultrasensitive, or potentially more stoichiometric, process compared to trans-activation.
source: These results suggest that cis-inhibition is a less ultrasensitive, or potentially more stoichiometric, process compared to trans-activation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of Hill coefficients for cis-inhibition and trans-activation.
